objective: V4.3.3 Legacy Memory Final Drain - finish converting valuable memory_items into sparks, demote safe legacy rows, and define the protected receipt policy needed for sparks to be the only living cognitive log.
context: V4.3.2 locked spark-first corpus expansion with 211 lineage sparks, 6 active sparks, and no memory_items deletion. Current live state before this packet: 2547 total memory_items; 1014 active; 104 archived; 1 stale; 1335 merged; 75 staged; 18 rejected. Coverage report shows 812 active memory_items without spark lineage, 42 remaining valuable migration candidates (Tier A 1, Tier B 31, Tier C 10), and 351 rows currently safe to demote by existing rules (167 archive as Tier D noise, 184 stale because they already have candidate spark lineage). 499 active rows are protected, mostly ticket-linked handoff receipts and pinned/canon rows, and need explicit policy before they can leave living memory.
decisions: Cursor implements all V4.3.3 tickets before V4.4 #363 is claimed.
Goal is one living cognitive log: sparks. memory_items remain audit/canon/receipts only.
No DELETE of memory_items and no removal of the memory_items table.
Migrate the remaining Tier A/B/C candidates before broader demotion.
Promotion remains review-gated; ticket chatter and approval receipts must not become active memory.
Demotion applies only after dry-run evidence and bounded apply limits.
Ticket-linked handoff receipts require a specific closed-ticket/archive policy before bulk demotion.
Preserve auditability through linked tickets, lock docs, source_memory_item_id, lineage_json, and generated artifacts.
Do not change V4.3 retrieval scoring/lane/cap contracts, Actions registry contracts, or CROWLEY_VERSION.
non_goals: Hiding audit trail for ticket-linked handoffs
risks: Protected ticket-linked receipts continue to dominate active legacy counts
Over-aggressive cleanup archives useful current-state facts
Migration of final candidates duplicates existing candidate sparks
Promotion of old ticket chatter pollutes active memory
Archive policy removes operator-visible evidence needed for handoff review
Legacy fallback still appears in chat/API after final drain
qa_expectations: Each ticket must ship focused tests for its policy, bounded dry-run/apply artifacts, and DB count evidence. T5 must run V4.3.3 focused tests, V4.3 retrieval acceptance, Actions registry/tool contracts, py_compile for touched scripts, git diff --check, and full unittest discovery.
next_action: Run V4.3.3 before V4.4 #363. Cursor claims T1 first and proceeds sequentially. Do not start Spark Map UI or V4.4 chat wire until V4.3.3 T5 is approved.

approval.note: User wants memory_items cleared from living memory and sparks to become the single cognitive log before continuing the V4.4 chat wire.

tickets.title: V4.3.3 T4: protected ticket receipt archive policy
tickets.description: Define and implement a policy for ticket-linked handoff/project_update receipts so they are no longer living cognitive memory while preserving audit. Closed-ticket receipts may be archived only when their linked ticket is done/cancelled and the useful state is represented by a lock doc, active/pinned spark, or ticket event lineage. Pinned/canon remains protected. Produce a dry-run first, then a bounded apply only if the policy is deterministic. Files: memory_spark_migration.py, scripts/archive_migrated_memory_items.py or new scripts/archive_ticket_receipts.py, docs/MEMORY_HIERARCHY.md, tests/test_ticket_receipt_archive_policy.py. Depends on T3.
acceptance: Policy distinguishes audit receipts from living cognitive memory
Closed-ticket linked receipts can be archived only with ticket status evidence and summary/lineage evidence
Open/in_progress ticket-linked receipts remain protected
Pinned/canon rows remain protected
Dry-run reports eligible, protected, and blocked receipt counts
Apply is bounded and records every changed id and linked ticket id
No memory_items are deleted
Tests cover closed-ticket archive, open-ticket protection, and pinned/canon protection
